title: Sessions read their inbox at start and at each tool round; the old cross-machine paths are deleted

story.i_want_to: see my inbox when I start and new messages at my next tool round, with one way to reach a session on another machine
story.so_that: messages reach me while I work, and nobody uses ssh couriers or keyed channel posts any more

rationale: PRD R11: a busy session gets new inbox messages at its next tool round through a hook; the SessionStart TEAM CHANNEL block becomes the session's inbox read, which until release 7 also lists the repo's open handoff: posts (section 4); and free-text channel_post, session-message.sh, cross-machine SendMessage and the nudger's ssh pokes are replaced. Today claude-config's SessionStart hook renders recent channel posts and open handoffs (hooks/session-start.sh:406-703), a UserPromptSubmit hook polls for handoffs at most once per interval (hooks/channel-push-on-prompt.sh), cross-machine asks go through bin/session-message.sh, and CLAUDE.md tells sessions to use both. PRD R7 assigns this release the end-to-end path 'a message reaching an idle session on another machine'. These hooks live in claude-config until release 8 moves the factory half into this repo (PRD R10), so the hook criteria here are built as a claude-config change released with this release.

acceptance_criteria.description: The MCP server writes its holder credential (US-52.13) to $HOME/.claude/loopctl-holders/<session_id>.key with mode 0600 on register and on every rotation, and deletes the file on holder_end, so a hook of the same session can call the inbox as that holder.

claude-config hooks/session-start.sh replaces its TEAM CHANNEL block with an INBOX block: one GET /api/v1/inbox?project_id=<repo project> with the session's holder credential, rendering DMs, held-item threads and channel messages as nonce-fenced untrusted data with 512-byte previews and ids, followed by the open handoff: posts from channel_handoffs, then acking the positions it rendered.

A new claude-config PostToolUse hook, hooks/inbox-on-tool.sh, reads the inbox at most once per INBOX_POLL_SECONDS (default 20) per session, emits unread messages as hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext in the same fenced render, acks only after printing, and exits 0 silently on any failure (no credential file, curl timeout of 3 s, bad JSON).

claude-config deletes hooks/channel-push-on-prompt.sh, its UserPromptSubmit entry in settings.shared.json and hooks/tests/channel-push-canary.sh, and deletes bin/session-message.sh with hooks/tests/session-message-canary.sh after moving each caller (bin/fleet-watch.py, hooks/lib/session-triage.sh, skills/shepherd/SKILL.md) to message_send.
claude-config bin/fleet-nudge.sh loses its ssh remote arm: a sweep reports and nudges only its own machine, and the fleet view of other machines is fleet_dash's.

claude-config CLAUDE.md's 'Reach a session on another machine' says to use message_send to the work item (or a DM to a holder id) and the inbox tool, with SendMessage only for a session on the same machine, and 'Post the defaults you chose' says to send each default with message_send to the PR's work item instead of a keyed channel_post.

The end-to-end suite gains the path 'a message reaches an idle session on another machine': a session on host B registers as a holder and goes idle, a session on host A sends it a DM with message_send, B's runner receives inbox_wake and runs its wake adapter, and B's next inbox read returns the DM exactly once and, after its ack, nothing.

test_cases.name: holder credential file lifecycle
preconditions: mcp-server with a stubbed fetch and HOME pointed at a temp dir, CLAUDE_SESSION_ID=s1
expected_results: file s1.key with mode 0600 holding the first key, then the rotated key, then no file (node --test)

test_cases.name: SessionStart renders the inbox, then handoffs, then acks (claude-config canary)
preconditions: a local stub server answering /api/v1/inbox with one DM, one thread message, one channel message whose body contains a fake fence line, and /api/v1/channel/handoffs with one handoff; a credential file for the session
steps: run hooks/session-start.sh with the session's SessionStart JSON on stdin
expected_results: one INBOX block with the three messages inside a nonce fence the body cannot close, then the handoff, and one POST /api/v1/inbox/ack carrying the three seqs; no TEAM CHANNEL header

test_cases.name: tool-round hook: interval, ack after print, silent failure (claude-config canary)
preconditions: stub server; INBOX_POLL_SECONDS=20; a fake clock via the hook's state file
steps: run the hook twice within 20 s
run it after 21 s with one new DM
run it with the credential file removed
run it with a stub that sleeps 5 s
expected_results: first run reads; second makes no request; third emits additionalContext with the DM then acks; the last two exit 0 with no output

test_cases.name: retired paths are gone and nothing references them (claude-config canary)
preconditions: the claude-config tree after the change
steps: grep -rn for session-message.sh, channel-push-on-prompt and the fleet-nudge ssh arm's remote= assignment across bin, hooks, skills, CLAUDE.md and settings.shared.json
expected_results: no match; the sweep reports this machine only and never invokes ssh

test_cases.name: CLAUDE.md names message_send for cross-machine asks (claude-config canary)
expected_results: each names message_send; neither names session-message.sh, a keyed channel_post or cross-machine SendMessage

test_cases.name: e2e: a DM reaches an idle session on another host (mix e2e)
preconditions: the e2e harness and sandbox repo (README names table: end-to-end suite, release 2) with two runner hosts A and B; on B an interactive claude session started in tmux and left idle, registered as a holder
steps: from A, message_send {to_holder_id: B's holder, body: "e2e <nonce>"}
wait up to 60 s for B's runner to log inbox_wake handled by its adapter
read B's inbox with B's credential, ack, read again
expected_results: the DM with the nonce once, then an empty inbox; where the measured adapter for B's OS is NextTurn, the path asserts the wake log line and the read instead of the session's own turn, and says so in its output

technical_notes: Where it is built: AC-52.28.2-6 are a change in claude-config (hooks/, bin/, skills/, CLAUDE.md, settings.shared.json), on that repo's own branch and PR, released together with this release's loopctl branch (release/manifest.toml pins the factory pack version, README names table: release manifest). Release 8 moves the hooks into this repo's factory pack (README release block 52.50-52.55; PRD R10).

SessionStart today: hooks/session-start.sh:406-703 (TEAM CHANNEL injection; channel posts read :475, handoffs read :483, render :698-703). Keep the handoff rendering and its claim instructions (:588-593) until release 7; replace only the channel-post read with the inbox read and drop the client-side self-dedup, which the cursor makes unnecessary.

Tool-round hook: reuse the envelope of hooks/channel-push-on-prompt.sh (always-exit-0 trap, SAFE_SID validation, debug channel; :28-60) and kb-recall-on-prompt.sh's nonce-fenced render; register it under PostToolUse in settings.shared.json (:419). PostToolUse runs after every tool call, so the wall-clock interval is what bounds its cost.

Credential: the hook reads $HOME/.claude/loopctl-holders/<session_id>.key, matching the session_id in the hook's stdin JSON to the MCP process's CLAUDE_SESSION_ID (US-52.13 AC-52.13.8). A session whose MCP server has not registered yet has no file and the hook does nothing.

Callers of session-message.sh to move: bin/fleet-watch.py, hooks/lib/session-triage.sh, skills/shepherd/SKILL.md, CLAUDE.md line 31, README.md, docs/harness/xps13.md, bin/install-mac-creds-publish.sh and bin/mac-creds-publish.sh comments, hooks/tests/fleet-name-canary.sh (grep -rln session-message.sh in claude-config, 2026-11-19).

Nudger: bin/fleet-nudge.sh remote arm :265-340 (args :271, remote= :325, ssh :326-334); delivery is already local-only (:77, :975), so what goes is the ssh observation hop and its --local-only flag plumbing.

e2e: add the path under e2e/ in the shape release 2's harness uses; the idle session is started on B by the harness, not by the runner; the wake adapter used on B is whatever US-52.27a's measurement selected.

loopctl docs: docs/repo-coordination-bus.md section 5 (store-and-poll, no websockets) and section 3.3 (TEAM CHANNEL, turn-boundary pull) are rewritten to point at PRD R11: inbox by cursor, tool-round hook, runner wake, fleet_dash subscription.
non_goals: Deleting handoff posts, the handoff tool and channel_claims: release 7 (README names table: move verb).
Moving the hooks into this repo: release 8 (README release block 52.50-52.55).
Waking idle sessions (the runner side): US-52.27a.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.28.3: when loopctl is unreachable the hook exits 0 with nothing and acks nothing, so every message is delivered at a later tool round once the link returns.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.28.1 and AC-52.28.3: hooks hold only a copy of the credential and a poll timestamp; read positions live in loopctl's channel_cursors, so a session restart or a new machine reads on from the server.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.28.3: the hook acks only after printing, so a crash between read and ack re-delivers on the next round and never loses; AC-52.28.7 asserts the second read after an ack is empty.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.28.3: a 3 s curl timeout bounds each poll and the 20 s interval bounds how often a busy session pays it.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.28.7: a session on another machine is reached by holder id through loopctl and woken by its own machine's runner, proven end to end.

definition_of_done: On two fleet machines after claude-config sync: a session on x1 sends a DM with message_send to a session on minis that is busy running tools; the minis session shows the DM in its context within one tool round after INBOX_POLL_SECONDS.
grep -rn session-message.sh ~/workspace/claude-config returns nothing on every synced machine.
defaults: Tool-round poll interval: 20 s (INBOX_POLL_SECONDS); curl timeout 3 s (owner may change).
Holder credential file: $HOME/.claude/loopctl-holders/<session_id>.key, mode 0600, removed on holder_end.
